items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Eddie Tompkins, Trummy Young, Willie Smith and myself, that was the quartet.

ctx.x: Well what happened, and I’ll let him get to you right quick, about six months later, Eddie Tompkins, the lead trumpet player and this is very good for history too although it’s, we didn’t know all this was going to happen. I was singing with the quartet and the trio because I had replaced Sy and I could do that — I had studied all of that in school. And we were in Washington at the Howard Theater and we were singing “Ain’t She Sweet” you know that number — a big hit for Lunceford. And the quartet finished and…
Eddie, the trumpet player, walked out the door and we didn’t see him, I didn’t see him for weeks later. So they needed this trumpet player real fast.

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Gerald Wilson was rehearsing on trumpet, and Gerald called me about going.

ctx.x: So I told him I wanted to go to California, you know, and to get out of that cold weather. And Roy was coming out in California at that time. I think I mentioned this to you the other day. Roy Eldridge, he had a gig, Billy Berg's -- did I tell you about that?

Well, we spoke about that probably. Anyway, after that gig ended, this band was rehearsing to go to Hawaii for six weeks, and it was C. P. Johnson. He had the job. Gerald Wilson was rehearsing on trumpet, and Gerald called me about going. He says, come on and go. He says, a guy who's supposed to go, the trombone player, his name was Bedsel. He said, he has exams. He was studying to be a dentist, and he
had exams, and he said, just six weeks. Come on and go.
